outcome.technical: READER (plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_clause_coverage.py): new acceptance_reading(description) -> {shape, items}. It tries three shapes in order and the first that yields an item decides, so they never mix. (a) `parenthesised`: the old regex and slicing, moved unchanged into _sequence_items. (b) `line-numbered`: _LINE_NUMBER = (?m)^[ \t]*(\d+)[.)](?=\s|\Z), read by the same sequence rule. The text right after the marker counts as a line start, so `Acceptance: 1. x` opens item one (case cs1d). A number must be followed by whitespace, so `1.5` opens nothing. (c) `unnumbered`: body.strip() as ONE item when it is not empty. A marker followed only by whitespace, or no marker, gives shape None and []. acceptance_items() now returns acceptance_reading()["items"]. New reading_line(description, subject=None) returns the line for shapes (b) and (c) and "" otherwise. Docstrings say why each shape exists. WRITER (plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py): imports _clause_coverage (layer below, edge rendered into the guide's module map by `_deps.py --write-map`). _say_acceptance_reading() prints the line after the gate lines in single `add`, after the change rows in `scope` when --description was passed, and once per new task in `add --from-file` as `acceptance (P2.1): ...`. _decided_lines keeps lines starting `acceptance:` / `acceptance (`, so the default short output shows the line. THE REAL LINES, printed by the ar-block fixtures through the verb's own __main__: shape (b) `add` printed `acceptance: 2 items, read from a list numbered at line starts - the executor answers each`. Shape (c) printed `acceptance: 1 item, the whole unnumbered text after the marker - the executor answers it as one clause`. Shape (a) `Acceptance: (1) the first (2) the second` printed nothing new: `[audit-task] P1.3 added to P1 -- A task; written: docs/audit/audit-plan.json` / `gate: test (the phase's testGate, wide -- ...)` / the tdd WARNING / `ready now -- /audit:run P1.3`, and no acceptance line.
